observations: A solid black silhouette with outstretched arms and a wide-brimmed hat shape stands centered against a flat amber-orange field, its lower edge dissolving into a dense band of black grass marks.
Roughly two dozen short zigzag lines radiate outward from the silhouette's head and shoulders across the open orange ground on both sides, slightly denser on the left than the right.
A small orange signature mark sits in the lower-right corner, the only warm line element that breaks the otherwise strict black-on-orange two-tone scheme.
reading: The flat amber ground gives the black silhouette nowhere to recede, pressing it forward with unusual force. Zigzag lines scatter around the figure like static or alarm, neither decorative nor contained. The dense grass strip at the base anchors the form while the radiating marks pull outward — a push and pull that reads as unease held in a very spare palette.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, title neighbor nnxyz nnotb #89 shares the same silhouette-plus-zigzag language on a magenta ground, making the amber-versus-magenta contrast a clear point of comparison. Title neighbor nnxyz nnotb #87 was inspected but offers no useful formal link.

connections.reason: Both works place a black silhouette with radiating zigzag lines against a saturated single-color ground, but #89 swaps amber for magenta and adds yellow line detail inside the forms, sharpening the contrast with #88's strict two-tone restraint.

rawblocks #47 shares the same flat amber-orange ground, but fills it with layered color marks rather than a silhouette, making the two a study in how the same background reads under opposite mark-making density.

lookingQuestion: Where exactly do the zigzag lines stop, and does their distribution around the silhouette feel even or weighted toward one side?
ambiguities: Zigzag distribution appears slightly left-heavy on close inspection; the draft described it as even, which has been corrected.
